At N ≥ 5 N\geq 5 , base confidence drops and p ​ ( N + k ∣ P B ) p(N+k\mid P_{B}) increases, matching our PIH findings. Computing the Pearson correlation, we observe a moderately high ρ \rho between the base probability and confirmation to the prompt (computed per-sample), with ρ = 0.37 , 0.46 \rho=0.37,0.46 for Qwen-VL, and Janus-Pro, respectively, as well as a small positive correlation of 0.1 0.1 for LLaVA-OneVision. Overall, these results demonstrate that base probabilities are correlated with model behavior under prompt-image mismatches, suggesting that PIH is more prevalent when visual confidence is low. To better understand and reduce PIH, we aim to locate model components responsible for PIH.
